# Aha Dispute & Point Reversal

## Dispute Types
- Points not credited within the expected window.
- Clawbacks applied for referrals or wins.
- Redemption not delivered.

## Process
Raise a dispute in the portal under My Points > Raise Dispute with the
transaction reference. SLA is 5 business days.

## Point Reversal
Points are reversed where the underlying transaction is reversed: referral
exit within six months or invalidated cross-sell wins.

## Appeals
Unresolved disputes escalate to the Rewards & Recognition team with a
30-day review window.

Policy code: AHA-DIS-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards & Recognition team.

# Aha FAQ

## Common Questions
Q: How do I check my balance?
A: The dashboard shows the current balance and the next expiring tranche.

Q: Can I transfer points?
A: No, points are non-transferable. Giving to approved causes is supported.

Q: What if I leave the bank?
A: Unredeemed points lapse on the last working day. Redeem before exit.

Q: Are points taxable?
A: Redemptions may attract perquisite taxation as per prevailing rules,
reflected in payroll.

Policy code: AHA-FAQ-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards & Recognition team.

# Aha — Employee Rewards Programme

## What is Aha?
Aha is the employee-facing rewards and recognition platform. Points are
earned through business-aligned actions and can be redeemed for vouchers,
merchandise and experiences on the Aha portal.

## Earning Points
| Trigger | Points |
|---|---|
| Successful employee referral hired | 5,000 |
| Cross-sell win (per qualifying win) | 250 |
| Audit-clean month (branch or ops team) | 500 |
| CSAT topping the region | 1,500 |
| Certification pass (approved list) | 2,000 |

## Redemption
- Minimum redemption balance: 1,000 points.
- Points expire 24 months after being awarded.
- Redemption catalogue: Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra vouchers, curated experiences,
  branded merchandise.

## Anti-Abuse Controls
- Referrals that leave within 6 months are clawed back automatically.
- Fake cross-sell entries are flagged during quarterly audit and lead to
  point reversal and disciplinary action.

## Support
For Aha portal issues, raise a ticket via HResponse under `Aha > Portal`.
For point disputes, use `Aha > Point Reversal`.

## Structure

participants' consent.

Policy code: AHA-CAMP-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards & Recognition team.

# Agent Console Guide

## Layout
The console shows the customer card, interaction history, queue state and
next booking in one view.

## Wrap-Up
Agents dispose every call with a disposition code and a CRM summary before
the next interaction.

## Transfers
Warm transfers preserve context to the receiving agent. Cold transfers need
supervisor approval for priority queues.

## Compliance
Calls are recorded; scripts for disclosures and verifications are mandatory
where defined.

Policy code: AP-CON-2026-01 | Owner: Contact Centre Technology.

# Callback SLA Framework

## Slots and SLA
- Priority/Burgundy: within 15 minutes of the slot.
- Retail: within 60 minutes of the slot.

## Measurement
SLA is measured from slot start to agent connect. Misses count against the
SLA dashboard.

## Breach Handling
Breaches trigger automatic retry, supervisor alerts and root-cause review
for repeat patterns.

## Reporting
Weekly SLA dashboards publish by queue, topic and agent team.

Policy code: AP-SLA-2026-01 | Owner: Assisted Channels team.

# CSAT Survey Programme

## Trigger
An SMS survey follows every completed call and callback.

## Questions
One CSAT rating question, one agent-empathy question and an optional
comment.

## Targets
Channel CSAT targets are set quarterly. Results feed agent coaching and
process improvement.

## Closed Loop
Detractors receive a follow-up within 48 hours from the service recovery
team.

Policy code: AP-CSAT-2026-01 | Owner: Assisted Channels team.

# Call Disposition Codes

## Code Families
- RES: resolved in first contact.
- FUP: follow-up scheduled.
- TRF: transferred.
- CMP: complaint registered.
- CBK: callback booked.
- NR: no response / voicemail.

## Usage Rules
Every interaction requires one disposition code. Follow-ups must reference
the original interaction ID.

## Reporting
Disposition data feeds first-contact-resolution and repeat-contact metrics.

Policy code: AP-DISP-2026-01 | Owner: Contact Centre Technology.

# Escalation Matrix

## Levels
1. Agent: first contact resolution.
2. Team lead: within same day for unresolved cases.
3. Relationship manager: priority customers.
4. Grievance officer: regulatory or media-flagged cases.

## Timeframes
Each level carries a defined SLA. Missed timeframes escalate automatically.

## Documentation
Every escalation records reason, owner and next action in the CRM.

Policy code: AP-ESC-2026-01 | Owner: Assisted Channels team.

- Topic-based routing: accounts, loans, cards, wealth, complaints.
- Language preference support including English, Hindi and regional languages.
- SMS confirmation with a callback reference ID.

## Channels

# IVR Tree & Routing

## Inbound Structure
1. Language selection.
2. Service selection: accounts, cards, loans, wealth, complaints.
3. Authentication via account details or OTP.
4. Routing to the topic queue.

## Smart Routing
Repeat callers are routed to the same agent when available. Priority and
Burgundy customers bypass general queues.

## Queue Messaging

threshold.

# Callback Scheduling Guide

## Slot Booking
Customers pick a 30-minute window between 09:00 and 20:00 IST on the next
five working days.

## Confirmation
An SMS confirms the slot with a reference ID. The agent sees the booking in
the agent console.

## Rescheduling
Customers can reschedule up to 30 minutes before the slot via the app or the
confirmation SMS link.

## Missed Calls
Missed callbacks retry once automatically, then flag for supervisor
follow-up the next business day.

Policy code: AP-SCH-2026-01 | Owner: Assisted Channels team.

# Axis Phone — Callback Workflow

## What is Axis Phone?
Axis Phone is the assisted-service channel where relationship managers and
contact-centre agents can be requested to call the customer back at a chosen
slot.

## Requesting a Callback (customer path)
1. Customer selects `Axis Phone` in the assistant or on the mobile app.
2. Provides preferred slot (30-minute windows between 09:00 and 20:00 IST).
3. Provides callback number (defaults to the number on file).
4. Selects the topic — `Account queries`, `Loan advisory`, `Cards`,
   `Wealth advisory`, `Complaint`, `Other`.
5. Receives an SMS confirmation with the callback reference ID.

## Assignment
The workflow engine picks an agent by:
- Topic → queue mapping.
- Customer segment (Retail / Priority / Burgundy).
- Language preference (English / Hindi / Regional).
- Agent load balancing — least-active-eligible agent wins.

## SLA
- Priority / Burgundy: **within 15 minutes** of the requested slot.
- Retail: **within 60 minutes**.
- Missed callbacks trigger an auto retry once and are flagged for supervisor
  review.

## Post-Call
- Agent must dispose the call with a valid outcome code and add the call
  summary in the CRM.
- CSAT survey SMS goes out within 30 minutes of call disposition.

## Reference
`AP-CB-2026-01` · Owner: Assisted Channels team.

# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference
`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

## Safety Rules
- Only SELECT queries are generated; no writes or DDL.
- Row limits cap result sizes.
- Query timeouts kill runaway requests.
- Cost limits bind warehouse consumption per session.

customer identifiers unless the user's role permits them.

Every generated query, result and user interaction is logged with the
user ID and timestamp.

# Change Management (CR) — Standard Process

## Change Categories
| Category | Definition | Approval |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standard | Pre-approved template, low risk | Team Lead |
| Normal | Business change with a defined blast radius | CAB |
| Emergency | Production incident fix within 24 hours | Emergency CAB |

## Required Artefacts
Every CR must attach:
1. Business justification and scope.
2. Impact assessment (customer facing? cross-team? regulator? data-migration?).
3. Roll-out plan with owners.
4. Roll-back plan verified in the last drill.
5. Test evidence — unit, integration, UAT.
6. Communication plan (mailer templates, banner text).

## CAB Cadence
- Standing CAB every **Tuesday and Thursday, 16:00 IST**.
- Cut-off for CR submission is 24 hours before CAB.
- Emergency CRs are triaged on demand via the emergency channel.

## Blackout Windows
No non-emergency production changes during:
- Financial year-end (last 5 business days of March).
- Half-year close (last 3 business days of September).
- RBI mandated reporting windows.

## Reference
`CR-STD-2026-01` · Owner: Change Advisory Board.

# Change Request (CR) Standard

## Definition
A **Change Request** is any planned addition, modification or removal of a
production or production-adjacent component that could affect service
availability, integrity or compliance.

## CR Categories
| Category | Approval | Freeze windows apply? |
|---|---|---|
| Standard | Pre-approved template, no CAB | Yes |
| Normal | CAB approval | Yes |
| Emergency | Emergency CAB (E-CAB) | Yes, with waiver |

## Mandatory CR Fields
- Business justification.
- Impact assessment (services, users, data).
- Roll-back plan with owner and time budget.
- Test evidence (unit, integration, UAT sign-off).
- Communication plan.
- Downtime window (if any).

## Freeze Windows
No production CRs during:
- Financial year-end close (last week of March, first week of April).
- Half-yearly close (last week of September, first week of October).
- Regulatory reporting window (2 business days before submission deadline).

## Approval Matrix
| Change scope | Approver |
|---|---|
| Non-prod, single team | Team lead |
| Prod, single service | Service owner |
| Prod, cross-service or data | CAB |
| Regulatory / customer-facing | CAB + Compliance sign-off |

# Impact Assessment Checklist

## Dimensions
- Customer: which journeys and channels are affected.
- Systems: upstream and downstream dependencies.
- Data: schema, migration and retention impact.
- Regulatory: reporting and audit implications.
- Operations: runbook and support readiness.

## Scoring
Changes are scored low, medium or high risk from the assessment. Score
drives the approval route.

## Review
Assessments are reviewed by a peer outside the delivery team for bias.

Policy code: CR-IA-2026-01 | Owner: Change Management Office.

# Incident-to-Change Linkage

## Mandatory Linkage
Every production change must reference a change record; every change
record must reference the motivating incident, problem or feature.

## Traceability
The tool enforces bi-directional links between incidents, problems and
changes for audit.

## Analysis
Unplanned change volume by root cause is reviewed monthly to drive
prevention.

## Reporting
The Change Management Office publishes incident-change linkage metrics
to CAB.

Policy code: CR-LINK-2026-01 | Owner: Change Management Office.

# Post-Implementation Review

## Scope
Every normal and emergency change undergoes a post-implementation review.

## Review Questions
- Did the change achieve objectives without regression?
- Was the rollback plan needed; did it work?
- Were estimates accurate?
- What should be done differently?

## Timeline
Reviews complete within 5 working days for emergency and 10 working days
for normal changes.

## Outputs
Review outcomes update the risk register, templates and runbooks.

Policy code: CR-PIR-2026-01 | Owner: Change Management Office.

# Problem Management Policy

## Purpose
Problem management finds root causes behind recurring incidents and
prevents recurrence.

## Process
1. Trend analysis and problem identification.
2. Root-cause analysis with structured techniques.
3. Corrective action planning and ownership.
4. Verification and closure.

## Linkage
Problems link to related incidents and the changes that resolve them.

## Metrics
Recurrence rate, mean time to problem resolution and open-problem aging
are reviewed monthly.

Policy code: CR-PROB-2026-01 | Owner: IT Service Management.

# Release Management Policy

## Release Types
Major, minor and patch releases follow defined paths. Hotfixes use the
emergency change route.

## Release Train
Standard releases align to a scheduled release train with fixed windows.

## Entry Criteria
Code freeze adherence, test sign-off, rollback plan and runbooks are
entry criteria for production deployment.

## Post-Release
Release health is monitored for the defined period; defects are triaged
to hotfix or next release.

Policy code: CR-REL-2026-01 | Owner: Release Management Office.

# Rollback & Recovery Drills

## Drill Requirement
High-risk changes must have a rollback plan validated in a recent drill.

## Drill Types
- Tabletop: walkthrough of rollback steps and decision points.
- Technical: actual rollback execution in a staging environment.

## Frequency
Drills run at least quarterly for critical applications; evidence is
attached to the change.

## Gaps
Drill gaps are remediated before the change proceeds. Unremediated gaps
escalate to CAB.

Policy code: CR-RB-2026-01 | Owner: Change Management Office.

# Test Evidence Requirements

## Required Evidence
- Unit and integration test results.
- UAT sign-off by business stakeholders.
- Performance test results for changes affecting critical paths.
- Regression suite outcome.

## Standards
Evidence must be attributable (tester, environment, date) and attached
to the change record.

## Sampling
The Change Management Office samples evidence for quality; gaps return
the change to review.

Policy code: CR-TEST-2026-01 | Owner: Quality Assurance.

# Burgundy Private Banking

## Offering
Dedicated relationship coverage for UHNI clients: investment advisory,
credit solutions, structured products (where eligible) and succession
planning referrals.

## Eligibility
Entry thresholds are defined by investible assets or relationship value
per the published criteria.

## Services
- Multi-asset portfolio construction.
- Bespoke credit and banking solutions.
- Access to alternates and pre-IPO opportunities subject to eligibility.

## Governance
All recommendations follow suitability and distribution policies with
documented risk profiling.

Advisory note: private banking referrals require relationship-banking
approvals.

# Car Loans

## Product
Financing for new and pre-owned cars, including electric vehicles with
scheme-specific rates.

## Quantum and Tenure
Up to the prescribed percentage of on-road price for new cars, lower for
pre-owned. Tenure up to the prescribed years.

## Eligibility
Age, income stability and bureau profile within policy thresholds. Co-applicant
income may be combined.

## Charges
Processing fee, foreclosure charges post lock-in and documentation charges
per tariff.

## Process
Sanction based on income and bureau check, disbursement to dealer or
seller after hypothecation documentation.

Advisory note: compare on-road price funding vs ex-showroom funding for the
customer.

# Credit Card Variants

## Portfolio
- Entry cards for first-time users.
- Rewards cards with accelerated points on categories.
- Cashback cards for everyday spends.
- Travel and premium cards with lounge and milestone benefits.

## Eligibility
Age 21-65 (primary), income thresholds by variant, good bureau score and
internal policy checks.

## Features
Interest-free period up to the prescribed days, EMI conversion, balance
transfer (subject to policy) and fraud cover.

## Billing
Billing cycle and due dates are defined at issuance. Minimum amount due and
late-payment implications are in the cardholder agreement.

Advisory note: always disclose fees, charges and interest to customers
before recommending a card.

# Current Account Products

## Segments
Current accounts serve proprietorships, partnerships, companies, trusts and
societies.

## Variants
- Basic current for small businesses.
- Business current with bundled digital tools.
- Premium current for mid-corporates with dedicated RM support.

## Features
High transaction limits, cash management services, bulk payments, and
overdraft linkage subject to approval.

## Documentation
Business registration proof, KYC of all authorised signatories, board
resolution for companies, and trust deed for trusts.

Advisory note: quote transaction charges from the tariff schedule.

# Education Loans

## Purpose
Financing for recognised courses in India and abroad — tuition, hostel,
exams and related costs.

## Quantum
Up to the prescribed amount for domestic and higher amounts for select
institutions abroad, with collateral requirements as per policy.

## Moratorium
Course duration plus a prescribed grace period, during which simple
interest applies per scheme.

## Eligibility
Admission to a recognised institution, co-applicant (parent/guardian) and
collateral as applicable.

## Disbursement
Stage-wise directly to the institution or against fee receipts.

Advisory note: inform customers about interest subsidy schemes where
eligible.

# Fixed Deposits — Product Note

## Product Variants
- **Regular FD:** interest paid monthly / quarterly / on maturity.
- **Reinvestment FD:** compounded quarterly, single maturity payout.
- **Tax Saver FD:** 5-year lock-in, deduction under Section 80C up to ₹1.5L.
- **Senior Citizen FD:** additional 0.50% over the applicable card rate.
- **NRE / NRO FD:** available to NRIs subject to source-of-fund controls.

## Booking Channels
- Internet banking (retail).
- Mobile app.
- Any branch during business hours.
- Relationship manager for HNI customers.

## Premature Withdrawal
- Allowed on all variants except the 5-year Tax Saver FD.
- Penalty: 1.00% below the applicable card rate for the period run OR the
  booking rate, whichever is lower.
- Sweep-in FDs are broken in FIFO order to fund the linked savings account.

## Nomination
Nomination is mandatory. It can be captured at booking or updated later via
the branch or internet banking. Joint holdings must specify the operating
mandate (either or survivor / former or survivor / joint).

## Auto Renewal
Auto renewal defaults to `Reinvestment` at the prevailing rate for the same
tenure. Customers can switch this off during booking.

- Motor: comprehensive and third-party.
- Health: individual, family floater and top-up.
- Home: structure and contents.
- Travel: international and domestic.

## Bancassurance
Products are sold through the bank's approved insurer partners under the
corporate agency arrangement.

## Claims
Claims follow the insurer's process; the bank assists with documentation
and status follow-up.

## Code of Conduct
Advisors must hold required certifications and follow IRDAI advertisement
and disclosure norms.

# Gold Loans

## Product
Secured loan against gold ornaments, with quick turnaround.

## Quantum
Loan-to-value as per RBI-prescribed limits on the pledged gold value.

## Process
Gold appraisal at the branch by certified valuators, agreement execution
and immediate disbursement.

## Tenure and Repayment
Tenure up to the prescribed months with bullet or EMI repayment options.

## Security
Gold is stored in dual-custody vaults and insured. Non-payment leads to
auction after due process per policy.

Advisory note: always explain auction terms and interest structure clearly.

# Home Loan Products

## Product Range
- Purchase of new/resale property.
- Construction and plot loans.
- Home improvement and balance transfer.
- Top-up loans for existing borrowers.

## Key Parameters
Loan-to-value up to the prescribed RBI-permitted ratio, tenure up to the
prescribed years, and rate linkage to the benchmark as chosen.

## Documentation
Property documents with legal and technical evaluation, income proof and
KYC of all applicants.

## Tax Benefit
Principal under Section 80C and interest under Section 24(b) within
statutory limits — customers should consult tax advisors.

Advisory note: highlight insurance options and foreclosure terms.

# Mutual Funds — Advisor Playbook

## Product Suite
Axis Wealth offers execution-only and advisory access across the following
mutual fund categories:
- Equity: large-cap, flexi-cap, mid-cap, small-cap, ELSS, sector/thematic.
- Debt: liquid, ultra-short, money market, corporate bond, gilt, credit risk.
- Hybrid: aggressive, conservative, balanced advantage, multi-asset.
- International feeder funds (currency hedged and unhedged).

## Suitability Framework
An advisor must complete the customer's risk profile before recommending any
scheme:
1. Risk tolerance questionnaire (12 questions).
2. Time horizon and liquidity check.
3. KYC + FATCA declaration.
Recommendations must map to the resulting risk band (Conservative / Moderate
/ Aggressive). Deviations require written justification and a customer
consent letter.

## SIP Rules
- Minimum SIP: ₹500/month (except direct-plan schemes; check factsheet).
- SIP registration cut-off: 8 days before first debit date.
- Pause / cancel SIP: T-2 working days before the debit date.
- Skipping instalments is allowed up to 3 months in a rolling year without
  breaking the mandate.

## Exit Load Ready-Reckoner
- Equity funds: 1% if redeemed within 12 months of allocation, nil after.
- Liquid funds: graded exit load from day 1 to day 7 as per SEBI norms.
- ELSS: statutory 3-year lock-in — no early exit permitted.

## Advisor Do & Don'ts
Do: disclose commission, provide TER details, share KIM before purchase.
Don't: guarantee returns, make comparisons with fixed deposits without a
disclaimer, or process transactions without a signed suitability report.

## Reference
`FA-MF-2026-01` · Owner: Wealth Advisory desk.

# National Pension System (NPS) Guide

## Structure
NPS is a defined-contribution retirement scheme regulated by PFRDA with
tier-I (retirement) and tier-II (voluntary) accounts.

## Asset Classes
Equity, corporate bonds, government securities and alternate assets with
allocation caps per PFRDA rules. Active and auto choice available.

## Tax Benefits
Contributions under 80CCD(1)/(1B) within limits; employer contributions
under 80CCD(2).

## Exit Rules
On maturity, up to the prescribed percentage may be withdrawn lump-sum
with the balance annuitised.

## Suitability
NPS suits investors seeking market-linked, low-cost retirement
accumulation with annuitisation at maturity.

Advisory note: explain lock-in and annuity purchase requirement.

# Personal Loans

## Product
Unsecured term loan for salaried and self-employed customers.

## Quantum and Tenure
Loan amounts up to the approved multiple of income, tenure up to the
prescribed years, subject to policy.

## Eligibility
Stable income, employer category, bureau score and debt-to-income ratio
within policy thresholds.

## Charges
Processing fee, prepayment charges (post lock-in) and penal interest as per
the published tariff.

## Disbursement
Disbursement follows documentation completion, credit approval and
agreement execution.

Advisory note: recommend based on repayment capacity, not just eligibility.

# Portfolio Review Process

## Cadence
Portfolio reviews occur at least annually, and semi-annually for Priority
and Burgundy relationships.

## Steps
1. Reconfirm goals and risk profile.
2. Review asset allocation against the model portfolio.
3. Identify drift, underperformers and rebalancing needs.
4. Document recommendations and client decisions.

## Records
Review notes, suitability reports and consent records are stored in the
advisory system.

## Governance
Reviews are sampled by quality assurance for suitability compliance.

Advisory note: rebalance only with client consent and transaction-cost
awareness.

# Public Provident Fund (PPF)

## Features
- 15-year tenure, extendable in 5-year blocks.
- Deposit range from the statutory minimum to maximum per financial year.
- Interest compounded annually at government-notified rates.

## Tax Benefits
Deposits qualify under Section 80C; interest and maturity are exempt,
subject to prevailing rules.

## Withdrawals and Loans
Partial withdrawals from the 7th year and loans from the 3rd year subject
to scheme rules.

## Premature Closure
Allowed only for specified life events (medical, education) per scheme
conditions.

Advisory note: PPF suits long-horizon tax-efficient accumulation.

# Risk Profiling Framework

## Components
Risk profiling combines:
- Risk capacity: income, assets, liabilities, horizon.
- Risk tolerance: questionnaire-based willingness to bear loss.
- Experience: investment literacy and history.

## Bands
Conservative, Moderate and Aggressive bands map to model allocations.

## Re-Profiling
Re-profile on material life changes or at least every two years.

## Suitability Rule
Products outside the risk band need written client acknowledgment.

Advisory note: never skip profiling for transaction convenience.

# Savings Account Products

## Product Range
- Basic savings: zero-balance variant per RBI guidelines.
- Regular savings with tiered interest.
- Salary accounts with bundled benefits.
- Premium savings with lifestyle and banking privileges.

## Eligibility
Resident individuals, HUFs in select variants, and minors through guardians.
NRI variants are offered under NRE/NRO schemes.

## Interest
Interest is credited quarterly based on daily balances, as per prevailing
rates published on the website.

## Value-Adds
Debit cards, digital banking, sweep facilities and insurance covers vary by
variant and are detailed in the product one-pager.

Advisory note: confirm the latest features from the product master before
quoting to customers.

# Senior Citizen Savings Scheme

## Eligibility
Individuals aged 60 and above; 55-60 for those who retired under
superannuation/VRS within the prescribed rules.

## Features
- Tenure of 5 years, extendable once by 3 years.
- Quarterly interest at government-notified rates.
- Deposit limits per scheme rules; joint accounts with spouse allowed.

## Tax
Deposits qualify under Section 80C. Interest is taxable and subject to TDS.

## Premature Closure
Allowed with penalty after the first year except death cases.

Advisory note: compare SCSS with the Senior Citizens Savings and monthly
income options.

# Sukanya Samriddhi Account

## Purpose
Small-savings scheme for the girl child, opened before age 10 and operated
until she turns 21.

## Deposits
Minimum annual deposit as prescribed, maximum per year. Interest is
government-notified, compounded annually.

## Tax Benefits
Deposits under Section 80C; interest and maturity exempt under the scheme.

## Withdrawal Rules
Partial withdrawal (up to the prescribed percentage) for higher education
after age 18; maturity at 21 years or on marriage after 18.

## Operation
Operated by the guardian until majority, then by the account holder.

Advisory note: emphasise the lock-in before recommending.

# Term Insurance Products

## Product
Pure protection life cover for a chosen term and sum assured.

## Variants
- Level term: fixed cover throughout.
- Increasing cover: grows with inflation-linked steps.
- Return of premium: refund of premiums on survival (higher premium).

## Key Features
High cover at low premium, riders for critical illness and accidental death,
and tax benefits under 80C and 10(10D).

## Underwriting
Medical underwriting based on age, health disclosures and habits.

Advisory note: recommend cover of 10-15x annual income as a starting rule.

# Unit-Linked Insurance Plans (ULIP)

## Structure
ULIPs combine insurance cover with market-linked investment in equity,
debt or balanced funds.

## Key Parameters
- 5-year lock-in period.
- Fund switches allowed; charges include premium allocation, policy
  administration, fund management and mortality.

## Tax
Premiums under 80C (subject to conditions); maturity proceeds under
10(10D) subject to premium limits.

## Suitability
Long-horizon investors comfortable with market risk who want insurance
and investment in one product.

Advisory note: disclose all charges and compare with term-plus-MF
alternatives.

# Wealth Management Tiers

## Tiering
- Classic: entry wealth tier with branch-based service.
- Priority: dedicated RM and priority banking services.
- Burgundy/Private: bespoke advisory, family office support for UHNI.

## Services
Portfolio reviews, estate planning referrals, tax planning guidance and
preferential pricing.

## Suitability
Tiering is based on relationship value; products remain subject to
suitability and risk profiling.

## Governance
Advisory conversations are recorded and reviewed for mis-selling controls.

Advisory note: tier upgrades are based on total relationship value.

# Background: Know Your Customer (KYC)

Know Your Customer (KYC) is the collection of laws, regulations and guidelines
that require regulated financial businesses to verify the identity, suitability
and risks associated with maintaining a business relationship with a customer.
These procedures fit within the broader scope of Anti-Money Laundering (AML)
and Counter-Terrorism Financing (CTF) regulations.

Modern KYC frameworks are built on three pillars:

- **Customer Identification Program (CIP)** — legally mandated verification of
  any person or entity opening a new account, including name, date of birth,
  address and a government-issued identification number.
- **Customer Due Diligence (CDD)** — understanding the nature and purpose of a
  client relationship, developing a risk profile, and ongoing monitoring of
  transactions for suspicious activity.
- **Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD)** — extra checks for higher risk clients such
  as politically exposed persons (PEPs), cross-border correspondent banking
  relationships, or businesses operating in jurisdictions with strategic
  deficiencies in their AML/CFT regimes.

Regulated entities are required to maintain a written, risk-based KYC program
that: forms a reasonable belief that they know the true identity of every
customer; verifies identity within a reasonable time; checks the customer
against sanctions and terror watchlists; and retains records for a defined
period after account closure (typically five years).

Electronic KYC (eKYC) uses digital identity verification, biometric checks and
liveness detection to onboard customers remotely. In India, the Reserve Bank of
India first issued KYC guidelines for banks in 2002; video KYC (V-CIP) is
permitted for eligible savings account onboarding, subject to procedural
controls around live capture, random challenge and geo-tagging.

# Background: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a technique that enables large
language models (LLMs) to retrieve and incorporate new information from
external data sources at inference time, instead of relying solely on their
pre-training data.

At a high level, a RAG system operates in three stages:

1. **Indexing.** External data (documents, tables, knowledge graphs) is
   converted into vector embeddings and stored in a vector database.
2. **Retrieval.** For a given user query, a retriever selects the most
   relevant documents from the vector store. Reranking, hybrid search
   (sparse + dense) and late-interaction models such as ColBERT are common
   accuracy improvements.
3. **Generation.** The retrieved passages are supplied to the LLM through
   prompt engineering ("prompt stuffing"), so the model prioritises the
   retrieved context over its parametric memory when producing an answer.

RAG improves factuality, allows citing sources for verification, and removes
the need to retrain the base model when knowledge changes. It does not
eliminate hallucinations: models can still misinterpret retrieved context,
combine outdated and updated information, or generate false claims when
retrieval quality is poor ("RAG poisoning"). Robust RAG systems therefore
depend heavily on chunking strategy, retriever quality, reranking, and
downstream guardrails.

# Branch Operations Leave Planning Guide 2026

## Purpose

This guide helps Branch Operations teams plan leave without compromising coverage during peak periods such as month-end and regulatory reporting peaks.

## Planning Rules

Privileged leave needs at least 7 working days of notice and manager approval.

At least 70 percent of the team must be available during declared peak windows.

Backfill plans must be agreed before overlapping leave is approved.

## Seasonal Guidance

Anticipate demand around month-end and regulatory reporting peaks and open early leave planning.

Rotate preferred holiday weeks across the team from year to year.

## Manager Duties

Publish the unit leave calendar quarterly.

Review pending balances and prompt planned usage.

Escalate conflicts to the HR business partner.

# Gifts & Entertainment Policy

## General Rule
Employees must not accept gifts or entertainment that could influence, or appear to
influence, a business decision.

# Leave Policy — 2026

## Applicability
This policy applies to all permanent employees of Axis Bank across corporate offices,
branches and contact centres. Contractual and third-party staff are governed by the
terms of their engagement contracts.

## Types of Leave

### Privileged Leave (PL)
- 24 working days per calendar year, credited quarterly (6 per quarter).
- Can be availed up to 3 times a year.
- Minimum block of 3 continuous days per instance.
- Requests must be raised on the HR self-service portal at least 7 working days in
  advance for domestic travel and 14 working days for international travel.
- Unused PL carries forward up to a cap of 60 days.

### Casual Leave (CL)
- 8 working days per calendar year, credited on 1st January.
- Cannot be carried forward.
- Maximum block of 2 continuous days.
- Requires reporting manager approval; can be applied on the same day for genuine
  emergencies.

### Sick Leave (SL)
- 12 working days per calendar year, credited on 1st January.
- Medical certificate mandatory for any block of 3 or more continuous days.
- Cannot be carried forward.

### Maternity Leave
- 26 weeks of paid leave for the first two children.
- 12 weeks of paid leave from the third child onwards.
- Adoption leave of 12 weeks for children below 3 months of age.
- Requests must be raised at least 8 weeks before the expected date, with the
  medical certificate attached.

### Paternity Leave
- 10 working days of paid leave available within 90 days of the child's birth.
- Can be split into 2 blocks.

### Bereavement Leave
- 5 working days for immediate family (spouse, child, parent, sibling).
- 2 working days for extended family.

## Compensatory Off
- Employees working on declared holidays are eligible for compensatory off within 45 days.
- Compensatory off cannot be encashed.

## Encashment
- On separation, up to 60 days of PL balance is encashed at basic + DA.
- CL and SL are not encashable.

## Escalation
For any dispute regarding leave balance, raise a ticket on HResponse under
`HR > Leave Balance`. First-level SLA is 2 business days.

## Cycle Timeline
| Phase | Window | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Goal setting | 1 Apr – 30 Apr | Employee + reporting manager |
| Mid-year review | 1 Sep – 30 Sep | Employee + reporting manager |
| Self-appraisal | 1 Mar – 15 Mar | Employee |
| Manager appraisal | 16 Mar – 31 Mar | Reporting manager |
| Normalisation | 1 Apr – 15 Apr | Business-unit HRBP |

## Rating Scale
| Rating | Label | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Outstanding | Exceptional, sustained impact well beyond role expectations. |
| 4 | Exceeds | Consistently exceeds expectations across most goals. |
| 3 | Meets | Meets all critical expectations. |
| 2 | Partially Meets | Meets some but not all critical expectations. |
| 1 | Below | Below expected performance; performance-improvement plan triggered. |

## Normalisation
- Ratings are normalised at the business-unit level with recommended distribution:
  Outstanding <= 8 %, Exceeds <= 25 %, Meets 55 – 65 %, Partially Meets <= 8 %,
  Below <= 4 %.
- Deviations require CHRO sign-off.

## PIP (Performance Improvement Plan)

- HRBP reviews progress every 30 days.
- Continued rating of `Below` after PIP leads to separation.

# Provident Fund (PF) & Gratuity — Quick Reference

## Provident Fund
- Contribution: **12% of basic + DA** by the employee, matched by the employer.
- Employer contribution split: 8.33% to EPS (Employee Pension Scheme, capped
  on ₹15,000 basic) + balance to EPF.
- Interest is credited annually as declared by the EPFO.
- Withdrawals: partial withdrawals allowed for defined reasons (marriage,
  higher education, home purchase, medical emergency) subject to service
  tenure thresholds.
- Universal Account Number (UAN) is issued at joining and is portable across
  employers.

## Gratuity
- Payable on separation after continuous service of at least **5 years**
  (waived for death / permanent disability).
- Formula: `(Last drawn basic + DA) × 15 / 26 × completed years of service`.
- Statutory cap: ₹20,00,000 (tax-exempt limit).
- Paid within 30 days of the last working day; delays attract simple interest
  at the notified rate.

## Nomination
Employees must nominate their PF and gratuity beneficiaries within 30 days of
joining and update nominations after any life event (marriage, birth of
child, divorce).

## Related Forms
Download from `Download > HR > Statutory Forms`:
- `PF-NOM-1` — PF nomination
- `GRAT-NOM-2` — Gratuity nomination
- `PF-WD-31` — Partial PF withdrawal

## Purpose
This policy defines the criteria under which former employees ("alumni") may be
considered for rehire into Axis Bank.

## Eligibility
An alumnus may be considered for re-hire if all of the following are true:
1. The employee resigned or superannuated from Axis Bank in good standing.
2. There was no adverse audit or disciplinary finding at the time of exit.
3. A cooling period of at least 12 months has elapsed since the exit date.
4. The role being considered is at or below the last held grade at the bank.

## Non-Eligibility
An alumnus is NOT eligible for re-hire if any of the following are true:
- Exit was due to a "termination for cause" or breach of code of conduct.
- The employee is currently under a signed non-solicitation clause with a
  competitor and the clause is unexpired.
- Alumnus was identified as a "Do Not Rehire" during exit interviews.

## Approval Workflow
Every re-hire must be signed off by:
- HR Business Partner for the hiring unit.
- Business head at N-1 to CEO.
- Chief Human Resources Officer (CHRO).

## Compensation
- Compensation for rehires is decided based on the target role and market band.
- Prior tenure is counted only for:
  - Gratuity computation.
  - Long-service awards.
- Prior tenure does NOT confer any accrued privileged leave or accumulated PF.

## Exceptions
Exceptions must be endorsed by the CEO and are limited to strategic hires
(business heads, technology leadership, key regulatory roles).

# Guest Wi-Fi Access

## Purpose
Guest Wi-Fi provides internet-only access to visitors without exposing the
internal network.

## Access Method
Visitors register with the front desk, receive a time-bound access code,
and connect to the guest SSID.

## Limitations
Guest Wi-Fi cannot reach internal applications. Printing and file shares
are unavailable.

## Security
Guest traffic is isolated and monitored. Unauthorised use of guest access
for business data is prohibited.

Policy code: IT-GWIFI-2026-01 | Owner: Network Operations.

# IT Asset Management

## Asset Register
Every IT asset is recorded with a unique asset tag, user, location and
condition. Moves update the register.

## Custody
Assigned users are custodians and are responsible for reasonable care.
Transfers between employees route through IT.

## Audit
Physical and logical asset audits run annually. Unaccounted assets are
investigated.

## Disposal
End-of-life assets are decommissioned, data-wiped and disposed through
certified recyclers with documentation.

Policy code: IT-ASSET-2026-01 | Owner: IT Asset Management.

# IT Helpdesk — Standard Playbook

## How to Reach IT Helpdesk
| Channel | When to use | SLA |
|---|---|---|
| Self-service portal (Unidesk) | All standard requests / incidents | 4h – 2d depending on priority |
| Phone (extn 40040) | P1 outages only | Immediate |
| Vartalaap `#status` | Track existing ticket status | Real time |

## Password Reset
1. Open https://reset.axisbank.internal.
2. Complete MFA (Authenticator push).
3. Enter your employee ID.
4. Provide the answer to your secret question OR OTP on registered mobile.
5. Set a new password satisfying the policy:
   - Minimum 12 characters.
   - At least 1 uppercase, 1 lowercase, 1 digit, 1 symbol.
   - Cannot reuse the last 5 passwords.

If MFA is not enrolled, raise a ticket via Unidesk with your reporting
manager on CC. SLA: 4 working hours.

## VPN Access Request
1. Raise SR under `IT Helpdesk > Connectivity > VPN`.
2. Attach business justification.
3. Approval path: reporting manager → InfoSec → Network Ops.
4. Provisioning SLA: 2 business days.

## Hardware Issues
- Log a Unidesk ticket under `IT Helpdesk > Hardware`.
- Select the asset type (laptop / desktop / peripheral).
- On-site engineer visit SLA:
  - P1 (screen dead, keyboard dead, no boot): 4 hours.
  - P2 (battery drain, key dropping): next business day.

## Application Access
Requests for internal applications (Unidesk, Finacle, Kaleidoscope) are
raised via `IT Helpdesk > Application Access`. Access requires:
- Role justification from reporting manager.
- Data owner approval.
- InfoSec review (only for regulated apps).

- Playbook code: IT-HD-2026-02
- Owner: IT Service Management team.

# Laptop Issuance Policy

## Eligibility
Laptops are issued to all full-time employees in roles requiring mobility.
Desk-bound roles receive desktops unless approved otherwise.

## Configurations
Standard configurations are refreshed periodically: a base model for general
users and a high-spec model for developers and data roles.

## Refresh Cycle
Laptops are refreshed every 36 months. Out-of-cycle refresh needs business-head
approval and is reviewed by IT asset management.

## Return and Transfer
On role change or exit, the device returns to IT for re-imaging. Data is wiped
using certified erasure before reissue.

## Damage and Loss
Accidental damage follows the repair process. Loss must be reported within 24
hours with an FIR where required; recovery charges may apply.

Policy code: IT-LAP-2026-01 | Owner: End-User Computing.

# Laptop Upgrade Policy

## Upgrade Triggers
- Device older than 36 months.
- Performance issues verified by IT diagnostics.
- Role change requiring higher specifications.

## Request Flow
Raise a Unidesk request under IT Helpdesk > Hardware > Upgrade with business
justification. IT diagnostics confirm the requirement.

## Approval
Standard upgrades approve via the reporting manager. Out-of-cycle upgrades
require business-head approval.

## Swap Process
The old device is returned, data is migrated by IT, and the new device is
issued within 5 business days of approval.

Policy code: IT-LAP-U-2026-01 | Owner: End-User Computing.

# Mailbox Quota Management

## Default Quota
Standard mailboxes receive the published default quota. Higher quotas need
manager approval.

## Archiving
The mail archiving service offloads older mail automatically. Users can also
archive manually via the client.

## Over-Quota Behaviour
At 90 percent usage, users receive warnings. At 100 percent, sending is
blocked until space is freed.

## Shared Mailboxes
Shared mailboxes carry team quotas and must have a named owner who
reviews access quarterly.

Policy code: IT-MBQ-2026-01 | Owner: Collaboration Services.

# Corporate Mobile Device Policy

## Issuance
Corporate mobile devices are issued to roles requiring mobility or
on-call availability, per the eligibility list.

## Management
Devices enrol in mobile device management with enforced passcode, remote
lock and wipe capability.

## Usage
Devices are for business use. Personal apps are limited to the approved
store. International roaming needs approval.

## Loss Reporting
Report loss within 24 hours; the device is remotely wiped. Repeated loss
may attract cost recovery.

Policy code: IT-MDM-2026-01 | Owner: End-User Computing.

# Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)

## Mandatory MFA
MFA is mandatory for email, VPN, HR systems and all privileged access.
Enrolment happens at onboarding via the authenticator app.

## Methods
Authenticator push is primary; hardware tokens serve users without approved
mobile devices.

## Lockout
Repeated MFA failures lock the account temporarily. Users regain access via
the self-service portal or helpdesk verification.

## New Device

# Network Troubleshooting Playbook

## Wi-Fi / LAN Not Working
1. Check the physical cable / dock is seated firmly.
2. `Windows key + I → Network & Internet → Advanced → Network reset`.
3. Try a different port or the guest wifi to isolate infra vs. laptop.
4. If still failing, open Unidesk under `IT Helpdesk > Connectivity > Wired/Wireless`.

## VPN Disconnect Loop
- Confirm you are on the corporate VPN group in Anyconnect (not the guest
  group).
- Toggle **Airplane mode** for 10 seconds to refresh the network stack.
- Clear the VPN posture cache (`%ProgramData%\Cisco\AnyConnect\posture\ISEPosture.cfg`) and re-launch.
- If disconnects persist within 60 seconds of connect, log a P2 SR — likely
  a certificate issue.

## Slow Application Load
Order of triage:
1. Ping the app endpoint from a command prompt; RTT > 200ms indicates
   backbone congestion.
2. Check `Task Manager > Performance` — is disk I/O at 100%? Might be a
   background AV scan.
3. Check DNS — `nslookup finacle.internal` should return a 10.x address.
4. Clear browser cache & retry.

## Escalation Matrix
| Priority | Definition | SLA |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | Full site / branch down | 15 min response |
| P2 | Individual user, business-critical app | 2 hrs |
| P3 | Individual user, non-critical | Next business day |
| P4 | Enhancement / how-to | 3 business days |

## Reference
`IT-NET-2026-01` · Owner: Network Operations.

# Anti-Money Laundering (AML) — Operating Framework

## Purpose
The AML framework prevents the bank's channels being used to launder proceeds
of crime and to finance terrorism, in line with the Prevention of Money
Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002 and RBI Master Direction on KYC.

## Three Lines of Defence
- **1st line — Business units:** onboard customers correctly, monitor
  transactions, escalate red flags.
- **2nd line — Financial Crime Compliance (FCC):** owns the AML policy,
  runs the sanctions and PEP screening tools, files STRs.
- **3rd line — Internal Audit:** independently tests the framework annually.

## Customer Risk Categorisation
- **Low risk:** salaried resident individuals with no adverse hits.
- **Medium risk:** self-employed, high-net-worth individuals, non-resident
  individuals with low transaction velocity.
- **High risk:** NGOs, cash-intensive businesses, PEPs, customers in
  FATF-listed jurisdictions.

Risk category drives periodic KYC refresh frequency (see the KYC standard).

## Reporting Obligations
| Report | Threshold | Filing SLA |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cash Transaction Report (CTR) | Cash > ₹10L / day per customer | 15th of the following month |
| Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) | On red flag | 7 working days from detection |
| Counterfeit Currency Report (CCR) | Any incident | 7 working days |
| Cross-Border Wire Transfer Report (CBWTR) | > ₹5L | 15th of the following month |

## Training
All customer-facing staff must complete the annual AML e-learning by
30 September of each year. Non-completion is tracked as an audit finding.

# Data Privacy — DPDP Act 2023 Alignment

## What the DPDP Act Requires
The Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023 defines how personal
data of Indian citizens ("Data Principals") must be processed by any entity
("Data Fiduciary"). Axis Bank is a Significant Data Fiduciary and follows the
obligations below.

## Lawful Grounds for Processing
Bank processes personal data only on one of the following grounds:
- Explicit consent obtained through the customer journey.
- Legitimate use for the performance of a service the customer has requested.
- Compliance with applicable laws (RBI Master Directions, PMLA, income tax
  reporting).
- Employment obligations for staff data.

## Data Principal Rights
Customers can raise these requests through the customer portal or by writing
to `dpo@axisbank.com`:
- Right to information about processing.
- Right to correction of inaccurate data.
- Right to erasure (subject to statutory retention).
- Right to grievance redressal (30 day SLA).
- Right to nominate a person to exercise their rights.

## Retention
Customer KYC and transaction data are retained for a **minimum of 8 years**
after account closure per PMLA. Beyond that, data is anonymised or purged
unless a legal hold is in effect.

## Data Breach Handling
Any suspected breach must be reported to the DPO within 24 hours by raising
a `Priority-Zero` incident on Unidesk. The DPO reports notifiable breaches to
the Data Protection Board within 72 hours.

## Reference
`LAW-DPDP-2026-01` · Owner: Data Protection Office (DPO).

# Insider Trading Policy

## Regulatory Basis
The policy implements the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations,
2015 for employees with access to unpublished price-sensitive information (UPSI).

## UPSI
UPSI includes unpublished financial results, capital actions, mergers,
acquisitions and major business developments.

## Trading Windows
Trading in the bank's securities is permitted only during open windows announced
by the compliance team. Closed windows apply around results and major events.

## Pre-Clearance
Designated persons require pre-clearance for trades above the threshold and must
hold positions for the prescribed minimum period.

## Disclosures
Designated persons file initial and continuous disclosures of holdings and trades
as required by the regulations.

Policy code: LAW-INSIDER-2026-01 | Owner: Compliance.

# Information Technology Act Obligations

## Regulatory Basis
The Information Technology Act, 2000 (as amended) governs electronic records,
cyber-security obligations and intermediary responsibilities.

## Electronic Records
The bank maintains legally valid electronic records with audit trails for
transactions, authentication events and disclosures.

## Cyber-Security Directions
The bank follows RBI cyber-security directions including incident reporting
timelines, security operations and board-level oversight.

## Incident Reporting
Cyber incidents are reported to CERT-In within prescribed timelines, with
preservation of logs and evidence.

## Awareness
Annual cyber-awareness training is mandatory for all employees.

Policy code: LAW-ITACT-2026-01 | Owner: Information Security.

# Know Your Customer (KYC) Standard

## Purpose
This standard defines the mandatory identity and address verification a
banker must perform before onboarding any customer, in line with the RBI
Master Direction on KYC.

## Acceptable Officially Valid Documents (OVDs)
- Aadhaar (with masked number, per UIDAI guideline).
- PAN.
- Passport.
- Driving licence issued by an RTO.
- Voter ID issued by ECI.
- Job card issued by NREGA duly signed by the state government.

## Video KYC (V-CIP)
V-CIP is available for eligible savings account onboarding subject to:
- Genuine live video with the customer visible from mid-torso up.
- Random challenge (e.g., "Show your OVD now").
- Officer capturing at least 3 still frames during the call.
- Geo-tagging of the customer's location.

## Periodic Update Frequency
| Risk Category | Frequency |
|---|---|
| High risk | Every 2 years |
| Medium risk | Every 8 years |
| Low risk | Every 10 years |

## Deficient KYC
Accounts flagged with deficient KYC are moved to `PARTIAL FREEZE` after
two written reminders. All debits (excluding regulatory / statutory dues)
are blocked in this state.

## References
- Policy code: LAW-KYC-2026-01
- Aligned to RBI Master Direction on KYC (as amended).
- Owner: Compliance — Financial Crime unit.

# Legal Hold Process

## Trigger Events
Litigation notice, regulatory enquiry, audit requirement or anticipated
dispute triggers a legal hold.

## Hold Notice
Legal issues a hold notice identifying custodians, systems and records in
scope. Custodians must preserve all relevant data.

## Scope
Email, documents, chat, databases and paper records related to the matter.

## Release
On matter closure, Legal issues a release notice and normal retention resumes.

## Non-Compliance
Failure to preserve under a hold is escalated as a compliance breach.

Policy code: LAW-HOLD-2026-01 | Owner: Legal.

# Market Conduct Standards

## Fair Dealing
Products and communications must be fair, transparent and non-misleading.
Employees must not make promises outside approved product features.

## Suitability
Sales follow the suitability framework: risk profiling, need analysis and
appropriate product mapping with documented consent.

## Grievance Readiness
Customers receive clear pre-contractual disclosures including terms, charges
and grievance channels.

## Mis-selling
Mis-selling attracts disciplinary action and may be reported to regulators.

Policy code: LAW-MC-2026-01 | Owner: Compliance.

# Negotiable Instruments Essentials

## Scope
The Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 governs cheques, promissory notes and
bills of exchange.

## Cheque Dishonour
Dishonoured cheques attract penalties and may lead to proceedings under
Section 138 upon statutory notice and non-payment within 15 days.

## Endorsement
Instruments are negotiated by endorsement and delivery. The bank verifies
endorsements per prescribed procedures.

## Paying Bank Duties
Payment in due course protects the bank. Alterations material to the instrument
render it invalid unless authenticated.

## Training
Ops staff complete annual NI Act refreshers on dishonour handling and returns.

Policy code: LAW-NI-2026-01 | Owner: Operations Compliance.

# Outsourcing Governance Guidelines

## Regulatory Basis
Outsourcing of material activities follows RBI guidelines on outsourcing of
financial services.

## Materiality Assessment
Activities are assessed for materiality based on impact on customers, data
confidentiality, regulatory reporting and business continuity.

## Board Oversight
Material outsourcing arrangements are approved by the board or its committee.
The outsourcing policy is reviewed annually.

## Service Provider Management
SLAs, audit rights, sub-contracting restrictions and exit clauses are mandated
in contracts.

## Records
The register of outsourcing arrangements is maintained centrally and available
to auditors and supervisors.

Policy code: LAW-OS-2026-01 | Owner: Compliance.

# Payment Systems Overview

## Regulatory Basis
Payment operations follow the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 and
RBI directions on digital payments.

## Authorisation
The bank operates approved payment systems — UPI, NEFT, RTGS, cards and wallets
— under board-approved policies.

## Customer Protection
Limits, cooling periods and dispute timelines follow RBI circulars. Unauthorised
transaction liability follows the zero/limited-liability framework.

## Operational Resilience
Payment systems maintain defined availability targets, fallback arrangements
and regular recovery drills.

## Reporting
Periodic returns and incident notifications are filed with the RBI within
prescribed timelines.

Policy code: LAW-PSS-2026-01 | Owner: Payments Compliance.

# PMLA Obligations Overview

## Regulatory Basis
The Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 obligates the bank to detect,
deter and report money-laundering activity.

## Reporting Officers
The Principal Officer is responsible for filings with FIU-IND. Every business
unit designates a compliance liaison.

## Transaction Monitoring
Automated and rule-based monitoring flags unusual patterns: structuring,
rapid movement, high-risk jurisdiction flows and unexpected activity.

## Reporting Obligations
Cash Transaction Reports, Suspicious Transaction Reports, Counterfeit Currency
Reports and Cross-Border Wire Transfer Reports are filed within statutory
timelines.

## Training
All customer-facing staff complete annual AML training; completion is tracked
and audited.

Policy code: LAW-PMLA-2026-01 | Owner: Financial Crime Compliance.

# KYC Master Direction Essentials

## Regulatory Basis
Customer onboarding follows the RBI Master Direction on Know Your Customer,
2016 (as amended).

## CDD at Onboarding
- Identify and verify the customer using Officially Valid Documents.
- Verify beneficial owners for non-individual customers.
- Assign a risk category: low, medium or high.

## Periodic Updation
High-risk customers: KYC refreshed every 2 years. Medium: every 8 years.
Low: every 10 years. Re-KYC is event-driven for significant changes.

## Enhanced Due Diligence
EDD applies to PEPs, high-risk geographies and high-value or complex
transactions, including source-of-funds checks.

## Record Retention
KYC records are maintained for the prescribed period after account closure as
per PMLA requirements.

Policy code: LAW-KYC-RBI-2026-01 | Owner: Compliance.

# Call Recording & Monitoring Standards

## Purpose
Calls in sales and service channels are recorded for quality, dispute
resolution and regulatory compliance.

## Disclosure
Customers are informed of recording through IVR announcements and in
channel terms.

## Storage
Recordings are encrypted, retained per the retention schedule and accessible
only to authorised roles.

## Usage
Recordings may be used for quality monitoring, training, investigation and
regulatory response. They are never shared outside authorised processes.

Policy code: LAW-CALLREC-2026-01 | Owner: Compliance.

# SARFAESI Overview for Staff

## Regulatory Basis
The Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of
Security Interest Act, 2002 enables secured creditors to enforce security
interests without court intervention.

## Key Stages
- Classification of the account as NPA.
- Demand notice under Section 13(2) with a 60-day period.
- Possession, sale or transfer of secured assets if dues remain unpaid.

## Borrower Remedies
Borrowers may object to the notice, seek account review, and approach the
Debts Recovery Tribunal within prescribed timelines.

## Staff Conduct
Only trained recovery staff handle SARFAESI actions. Fair-practices codes for
recovery agents are strictly followed.

Policy code: LAW-SARFAESI-2026-01 | Owner: Legal.

# Subpoena & Regulatory Notice Handling

## Receipt
All court summons, subpoenas, and regulatory requisitions route through the
central legal intake inbox within 24 hours of receipt.

## Response Ownership
Legal coordinates with business, compliance and operations to compile
responses. Internal deadlines are set at least three days before external
deadlines.

## Confidentiality
Only authorised personnel handle the matter. Responding parties are restricted
to named custodians.

## Record-Keeping
A register records the notice, response timeline, produced documents and
closure.

Policy code: LAW-SUBP-2026-01 | Owner: Legal.

# Third-Party Risk Management

## Scope
Applies to vendors, service providers, fintech partners and outsourcing
arrangements with access to bank data, systems or customers.

## Onboarding Diligence
Financial, operational, reputational, data-security and regulatory screening
before contract signing. High-risk categories require enhanced checks.

## Contractual Controls
Contracts include data-protection clauses, audit rights, business continuity
obligations and incident notification timelines.

## Ongoing Monitoring
Periodic re-assessment, SLA reviews and security posture checks. Critical
vendors are re-assessed at least annually.

## Exit
Off-boarding includes data return/destruction certification and access
revocation verification.

Policy code: LAW-TPRM-2026-01 | Owner: Vendor Risk Office.

# Vendor Due Diligence Standard

## Core Checks
- Incorporation and existence verification.
- Ultimate beneficial ownership identification.
- Sanctions, negative news and litigation screening.
- Financial health assessment.

## Risk Tiers
Vendors are tiered by spend, data access and criticality. Tier-1 vendors face
the full due-diligence scope.

## Documentation
Due-diligence packs are retained for audit and refreshed annually or on
material change.

## Failure Handling
Failed due diligence leads to engagement rejection or termination with
business continuity support.

Policy code: LAW-VDD-2026-01 | Owner: Vendor Risk Office.

# Whistleblower Policy

## Purpose
The policy enables employees and third parties to report suspected misconduct,
fraud, regulatory violations or ethical breaches without fear of retaliation.

## Channels
Reports may be submitted through the dedicated whistleblower portal, email or
postal address managed by the ethics committee. Anonymous reporting is permitted.

## Confidentiality
The identity of the whistleblower is protected to the extent permitted by law.
Breach of confidentiality by investigation teams is a disciplinary offence.

## Protection
Good-faith reports do not attract adverse consequences. Vexatious or malicious
complaints are themselves subject to disciplinary action.

## Investigation
The ethics committee triages and investigates reports, engaging Internal Audit,
Compliance or external experts as needed. Outcomes are reported to the Audit
Committee of the Board.

Policy code: LAW-WB-2026-01 | Owner: Ethics & Compliance.

Q: What is the leave policy at Axis Bank?
A: Employees are entitled to 24 privileged leaves, 8 casual leaves and 12 sick leaves per calendar year. Privileged leaves must be planned at least 7 working days in advance and can be availed up to 3 times a year. Unused privileged leaves are carried forward up to a cap of 60 days.
